t: Design Authentication Manager: Tracking Expiring Tokens with Absolute Deadlines
o: We manage authentication tokens that live for a fixed timeToLive seconds after creation or renewal. generate registers a token that dies at currentTime + timeToLive; renew pushes an existing unexpired token's death to the renewal time plus timeToLive; countUnexpiredTokens reports how many tokens are still alive. The subtle rule is that a token expiring at time t is already dead for any action taken at time t, so a token is alive exactly when expiry > currentTime. Trace Example 1 with timeToLive = 5: renewing aaa at time 1 is ignored because no token exists yet; generate aaa at time 2 sets expiry 7; counting at time 6 returns 1; generate bbb at time 7 sets expiry 12; renewing aaa at time 8 is ignored because aaa expired at 7; renewing bbb at time 10 succeeds (12 > 10) and moves its expiry to 15; counting at time 15 returns 0 because aaa died long before and bbb expires exactly at 15, which already counts as expired. Constraints cap calls at 2000 and guarantee strictly increasing currentTime, so even naive scans pass — but monotonic time also unlocks elegant lazy-cleanup structures.
k: A token is alive exactly when its stored expiry is strictly greater than currentTime: expiring at time t means dead before any action at time t.
Store absolute deadlines, not ages: generate becomes a single map write and every other decision reduces to one integer comparison.
Because currentTime strictly increases across calls, an expired token stays expired forever, enabling lazy cleanup with a min-heap of deadlines.
Renewing an unknown or expired token must be a silent no-op — skipping the strict expiry check before overwriting is the classic bug.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Map with Lazy Cleanup
a.i: Keep a dictionary mapping each tokenId to its absolute expiry. generate writes expiry = currentTime + timeToLive; renew overwrites only if the stored expiry is strictly greater than currentTime; counting simply scans the map and tallies entries with expiry > currentTime. Dead tokens linger until overwritten or purged, but they never affect correctness — only constant factors.
s: Store tokens[tokenId] = currentTime + timeToLive on generate.
On renew, ignore the call unless the stored expiry is strictly greater than currentTime; otherwise rewrite it to currentTime + timeToLive.
On countUnexpiredTokens, iterate over all stored expiries and count those strictly greater than currentTime (optionally erasing the rest to keep the map small).
a.t: Generate and renew are O(1); countUnexpiredTokens is O(T) over T tracked tokens due to the full-map scan — trivial with at most 2000 calls.
a.sp: O(T) — one map entry per distinct generated token id.

a.n: Approach 2: Hash Map Plus Min-Heap of Deadlines
a.i: Push (expiry, tokenId) into a min-heap whenever a token is created or renewed, keeping the hash map as the source of truth for each token's latest expiry. Since currentTime is strictly increasing, any heap entry whose expiry <= currentTime is permanently dead. When a count is requested, pop such entries, discarding stale duplicates whose recorded expiry no longer matches the map, and delete their owners; the live map size is then the answer. Every event enters and leaves the heap at most once, so work amortizes to O(log T) per call.
s: Maintain map tokenId -> latest expiry plus a min-heap holding one (expiry, id) entry per generation or renewal event.
cleanup(now): while the heap top has expiry <= now, pop it; if its recorded expiry equals the map value, remove that token from the map.
Run cleanup at the start of renew and countUnexpiredTokens, then answer directly (map membership test for renew, map size for count).
a.t: Amortized O(log T) per operation — each generation or renewal pushes one heap entry that is popped at most once; cleanup cost is charged to those pushes.
a.sp: O(T) — the map holds live tokens and the heap holds at most one entry per event ever issued.

w: Open with the plain hash map: it matches the specification almost line by line and passes comfortably within the 2000-call budget. Bring up the heap variant when asked to make counting cheaper than a full scan or to evict eagerly as time advances. Three details decide correctness: strict inequality at the expiry boundary (expiry equal to currentTime means dead), ignoring renewal of missing or already-expired tokens, and remembering that renew resets the deadline relative to the new currentTime rather than extending the old one. Likely follow-ups: an explicit delete(tokenId) operation (the heap entry becomes stale — the map cross-check shown here already handles it), or reporting the number alive at many historical timestamps, which pushes you toward a sorted container of deadlines.
